hints.S21_A1: The dash lists the proof: BRILLIANT REDS, GOLDS AND BLUES stretching across the wall. Ask: which word describes a surface full of many bright shades? 'Dull' is its opposite, 'small' is about size, and 'rough' is about touch.
hints.S21_A2: The sculptor is cutting into a BLOCK OF WOOD with a small KNIFE. Ask: which verb means to cut a shape out of something solid? 'Pour' needs a liquid, 'scatter' spreads things about, and 'assemble' joins ready-made parts.
hints.S21_A3: Mei had no blue paint left and had to MIX MORE FROM SCRATCH. Ask: which phrase means that every last drop has been used up? 'Given away' means handed over free, and 'put away' means simply stored.
hints.S21_A4: Omar WON FIRST PLACE and it was the PROUDEST MOMENT of his school life. Ask: does the idiom describe joy, illness, trouble or danger? An idiom carries one whole meaning; read it as a phrase, never word by word.
hints.S21_A5: The painting looked ALMOST LIKE A REAL PHOTOGRAPH, so its colours must be strong and sharply clear. Ask: which word means bright, rich and full of life? 'Dull', 'faded' and 'blurred' all describe the opposite.
hints.S21_B1: The subject is EVERYONE, not 'the art class'. Words like everyone and nobody act like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S21_B2: HAS stands right before the blank, and the studio exists now, THIS TERM. Ask: which form partners with 'has' to build the present perfect - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle?
hints.S21_B3: The ELECTRICITY SUDDENLY WENT OUT and cut into something already happening at the wheel. Ask: which choice shows an action in progress in the PAST? A plain past verb would only report a finished job.
hints.S21_B4: THAN compares this painting with all her earlier work, and the adjective being tested is a long one of three syllables. Ask: do long adjectives add -er, or take a comparing word in front? 'Most' is for the top of a group, and 'beautifuler' is not English.
hints.S21_B5: The artwork sits by one exact spot, THE MAIN ENTRANCE, so that every visitor passes it. Ask: which preposition points to a specific place-point? 'In' would push it inside the doorway, and 'on' would lay it flat against a surface.
hints.S21_B6: The statement uses the verb IS: 'The competition IS HELD every year'. Ask: after a POSITIVE statement, must the tag turn negative or stay positive? And should the tag keep the same verb rather than borrow 'do'?
hints.S21_B7: The MURAL cannot paint itself; a GROUP OF STUDENT VOLUNTEERS did the work. Ask: does the mural do the action or receive it? A receiver needs the PASSIVE, and three weekends that are over fix the tense in the past.
hints.S21_B8: The teacher TOLD the class about something they must avoid doing. Ask: after 'told + someone', which form follows - the plain verb, the -ing form, or the infinitive? And where does the word 'not' sit, before that little word 'to' or after it?
hints.S21_C1: ENJOYS is the verb standing right before the blank. Ask: after enjoy, love or finish, which form of the next verb do we use - the infinitive, or the -ing form? The pattern decides this, not the meaning.
hints.S21_C2: EVERY MONTH signals a repeated habit, and the subject HE is one person. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb with -s on the end?
hints.S21_C3: LAST SUMMER is finished time, and this verb is regular. Ask: which ending turns a regular verb into the simple past? The mural was completed, so no continuous form is needed here.
hints.S21_C4: WHILE he ________ the upper section, a RAIN SHOWER forced him to stop: a sudden event cutting into a longer one. Ask: which form shows the longer action still in progress, and which helper matches a single person?
hints.S21_C5: Count the subject: TWO OF HIS FRIENDS, more than one, and they worked AT THE SAME TIME as Grandfather. Ask: which past form shows an action still going on, and which helper belongs with a plural subject?
hints.S21_C6: WANTED is the verb in front of the blank: 'Grandfather always WANTED ________ a mural'. Ask: after want, hope or plan, which form follows - the -ing form, the bare plain form, or the infinitive with its little partner word in front?
hints.S21_C7: CAN is a modal verb, and modals never let the following verb change shape. Ask: after can, should or must, do we use the -s form, the -ing form, or the bare plain form with nothing added at all?
hints.S21_C8: RIGHT NOW points at this very moment, and GRANDFATHER means one person. Ask: which form shows an action happening as you read, and which helper goes with a singular subject? A simple present verb would only describe a habit.
hints.S21_D1: The dash defines it: A QUICK PENCIL DRAWING that plans out the picture, made BEFORE PAINTING. Ask: which box word names that rough first drawing? A portrait is a finished picture of a person, not a plan.
hints.S21_D2: Read the definition after the comma: A PIECE OF CLOTH stretched tightly over a WOODEN FRAME. Ask: which box word names that cloth? An easel only holds the work upright, and a palette is where the colours are mixed.
hints.S21_D3: The clue is how a surface FEELS TO THE TOUCH: ROUGH, SMOOTH, BUMPY or SOFT. Ask: which box word names that quality of a surface? This one is about the fingers, not about the colours.
hints.S21_D4: The dash explains it: THE SPARK OF CREATIVITY that makes an artist WANT TO BEGIN, and it may come from nature or from a stranger's face. Ask: which box word names that first push of an idea?
hints.S21_D5: Once enough pieces are finished, the artist wants THE PUBLIC to COME AND VIEW THE WORK. Ask: which box word names a public display of artworks? The blank follows 'an', so the word must begin with a vowel sound.
hints.S21_E1: Try reading the underlined word as 'not any' - it makes no sense in front of WHERE TO BEGIN. Ask: which spelling means to have knowledge in your head? The two sound alike, so choose by meaning, never by sound.
hints.S21_E2: CUTING has only one T. Look at the plain verb 'cut': one short vowel, one final consonant. Ask: before -ing, does that consonant double, or stay single? Think of run and sit, and follow the same rule.
hints.S21_E3: Find the real subject: THE ART SUPPLIES - brushes, paints and paper, so more than one thing. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular verb or the plural one? Match the verb to the subject, not to the sound of the phrase.
hints.S21_E4: LEAFS just adds -s. Look at the ending of the singular word: the letter -f. Ask: what happens to that -f before the plural ending? Think of knife and half, and make the same change here.
hints.S21_E5: The PAINTINGS belong to the pupils, so the word must show ownership, not just number. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? And where does the apostrophe go when the owners are many?
hints.S21_F1: Two facts, one rule: MIX YELLOW AND BLUE PAINT and the result always follows. Ask: which little word joins a condition to its result? And in a general truth, do both halves stay in the simple present, or does one take 'will'?
hints.S21_F2: 'HAVE YOU EVER MIXED your own colours?' is a yes/no question. Ask: which small joining word follows ASKED? Does the question keep its inverted order, or become a normal statement? And what must happen to 'you' and to the tense?
